# Long and short regressions

## Model and two estimators of $\beta_1$

::: {.hidden}
\gdef\E#1{\mathrm{E}\left[#1\right]}
\gdef\Var#1{\mathrm{Var}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\Cov#1{\mathrm{Cov}\left(#1\right)}
\gdef\rank#1{\operatorname{rank}\left(#1\right)}
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
# Figures are drawn through tikzDevice, so every label is typeset by LaTeX
# itself and matches the mathematics in the slides. Needs tikzDevice, png and
# a working pdflatex and pdftoppm.
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tikzDevice))
# Keep the string-metrics cache out of the source folder.
options(tikzMetricsDictionary = file.path(tempdir(), "tikzMetrics"))

tikz_fig <- function(stem, width, height, expr, draw = TRUE) {
  d <- file.path(tempdir(), "tikzfig")
  dir.create(d, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  tex <- file.path(d, paste0(stem, ".tex"))
  tikz(tex, width = width, height = height, pointsize = 11, standAlone = TRUE)
  expr
  dev.off()
  system2("pdflatex", c("-interaction=batchmode", "-halt-on-error",
                        paste0("-output-directory=", shQuote(d)), shQuote(tex)),
          stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
  system2("pdftoppm", c("-r", "300", "-png", "-singlefile",
                        shQuote(file.path(d, paste0(stem, ".pdf"))),
                        shQuote(file.path(d, stem))),
          stdout = FALSE, stderr = FALSE)
  img_path <- file.path(d, paste0(stem, ".png"))
  if (!draw) return(img_path)
  img <- png::readPNG(img_path)
  op <- par(mar = rep(0, 4))
  plot.new(); plot.window(c(0, 1), c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  rasterImage(img, 0, 0, 1, 1, interpolate = TRUE)
  par(op)
  invisible(NULL)
}

# A picture the class builds up on the board. In the slide show the frames
# share one grid cell and appear one by one as fragments, so advancing or going
# back uses Reveal's normal fragment controls without shifting the figure; in
# ordinary HTML and PDF the complete picture is drawn once. `drawer(step)`
# draws the frame for `step`; `cls` names the grid cell, so two such pictures
# in one deck do not collide.
build_frames <- function(cls, stem, steps, descriptions, width, height, drawer) {
  if (!identical(knitr::opts_knit$get("rmarkdown.pandoc.to"), "revealjs")) {
    tikz_fig(stem, width, height, drawer(max(steps)))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  cat('```{=html}\n<style>\n',
      '.reveal .', cls, ' { display: grid; width: ', round(96 * width),
      'px; max-width: 100%; margin: 1em auto; }\n',
      '.reveal .', cls, ' > img { grid-area: 1 / 1; width: 100%; max-width: 100%; ',
      'max-height: none; margin: 0; background: white; transition: none; }\n',
      '</style>\n<div class="', cls, '">\n', sep = "")
  for (j in seq_along(steps)) {
    frame <- tikz_fig(paste0(stem, "-step-", steps[j]), width, height,
                      drawer(steps[j]), draw = FALSE)
    cat(sprintf('<img class="%s" src="%s" alt="%s">\n',
                if (j == 1L) "" else "fragment",
                knitr::image_uri(frame), descriptions[j]))
  }
  cat('</div>\n<script>\n',
      'document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {\n',
      '  const diagram = document.querySelector(".', cls, '");\n',
      '  const parentFragment = diagram.closest(".fragment");\n',
      '  function keepDiagramVisible(event) {\n',
      '    if (diagram.contains(event.fragment) ||\n',
      '        (event.type === "fragmentshown" && event.fragment === parentFragment)) {\n',
      '      diagram.scrollIntoView({ block: "center", behavior: "instant" });\n',
      '    }\n',
      '  }\n',
      '  Reveal.on("fragmentshown", keepDiagramVisible);\n',
      '  Reveal.on("fragmenthidden", keepDiagramVisible);\n',
      '});\n</script>\n```\n', sep = "")
  invisible(NULL)
}

red <- "#d7301f"; blue <- "#1f78b4"

# The class's picture of bias against variance: two square panels with the
# same window, each holding 40 simulated draws of a two-dimensional estimate
# of beta_1 = (0, 0), seed 527. Left, the long regression's estimate, drawn
# from N(beta_1, I_2): centred on beta_1 and wide. Right, the short
# regression's estimate, drawn from N(beta_1 + bias, 0.09 I_2) with
# bias = (1.1, 0.8): tight and centred off beta_1. The cross marks beta_1.
# Built up in two frames, as on the board: step 1 draws the long regression's
# panel and leaves the right half blank; step 2 adds the short regression's panel.
bias_variance_picture <- function(step = 2L) {
  set.seed(527)
  m <- 40; b1 <- c(0, 0); bias <- c(1.1, 0.8); sd_long <- 1; sd_short <- 0.3
  long <- cbind(rnorm(m, b1[1], sd_long), rnorm(m, b1[2], sd_long))
  short <- cbind(rnorm(m, b1[1] + bias[1], sd_short),
                 rnorm(m, b1[2] + bias[2], sd_short))
  op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(0.3, 0.3, 1.6, 0.3), pty = "s")
  panel <- function(pts, lab, col, show) {
    plot.new(); plot.window(xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3, 3), asp = 1)
    if (!show) return(invisible(NULL))
    box()
    points(pts[, 1], pts[, 2], pch = 16, cex = 0.7, col = col)
    points(b1[1], b1[2], pch = 3, cex = 1.6, lwd = 2.5)
    text(b1[1] - 0.3, b1[2], "$\\beta_1$", adj = c(1, 0.5))
    mtext(lab, side = 3, line = 0.3, cex = 1.1)
  }
  panel(long, "$\\hat\\beta_1$", blue, TRUE)
  panel(short, "$\\tilde\\beta_1$", red, step >= 2L)
  par(op)
}
```

- Two blocks of regressors, $k_1 + k_2 = k$:
  $$
  Y = \underset{n\times k_1}{X_1}\ \underset{k_1\times 1}{\beta_1} + \underset{n\times k_2}{X_2}\ \underset{k_2\times 1}{\beta_2} + U, \qquad X = [\, X_1 \ \ X_2 \,]
  $$

- Assumptions 2, 3 and 4:
  $$
  \E{U \mid X_1, X_2} = 0, \qquad \Var{U \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 I_n, \qquad \rank{X} = k
  $$

- "Long" regression $Y \mid X_1, X_2$, controlling for $X_2$ (FWL):
  $$
  \hat\beta_1 = (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2 Y, \qquad M_2 = I_n - X_2 (X_2^\top X_2)^{-1} X_2^\top
  $$

- "Short" regression $Y \mid X_1$, not controlling for $X_2$:
  $$
  \tilde\beta_1 = (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top Y
  $$

## Short against long in the sample

- Long regression's fit (third lecture):
  $$
  Y = X_1 \hat\beta_1 + X_2 \hat\beta_2 + \hat U
  $$

- Substitute into $\tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde\beta_1 &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top Y \\
  &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top \big( X_1 \hat\beta_1 + X_2 \hat\beta_2 + \hat U \big) \\
  &= \hat\beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \hat\beta_2 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \underbrace{X_1^\top \hat U}_{=\,0} \\
  &= \boxed{\ \hat\beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \hat\beta_2\ } \\
  &\ne \hat\beta_1 \quad \text{in general} \\
  \tilde\beta_1 &= \hat\beta_1 \quad \text{if } X_1^\top X_2 = 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Omitting a relevant regressor

## Signal, bias and noise

- True model, estimated by the short regression $Y \mid X_1$:
  $$
  Y = X_1 \beta_1 + X_2 \beta_2 + U, \qquad \beta_2 \ne 0
  $$

- Substitute the true model into $\tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde\beta_1 &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top Y \\
  &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top \big( X_1 \beta_1 + X_2 \beta_2 + U \big) \\
  &= \underbrace{\beta_1}_{\text{signal}} + \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \beta_2}_{\text{bias}} + \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top U}_{\text{noise}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Conditional mean of $\tilde\beta_1$, by Assumption 2:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \beta_2 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top \underbrace{\E{U \mid X_1, X_2}}_{=\,0} \\
  &= \boxed{\ \beta_1 + \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \beta_2}_{\text{bias}}\ } \\
  &\ne \beta_1 \quad \text{in general}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Bias $= 0$ if:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{1.}\quad & \beta_2 = 0 \\
  \text{2.}\quad & X_1^\top X_2 = 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Example: return to education, ability omitted

- Wage equation, $k_1 = k_2 = 1$:
  $$
  \ln \text{Wage}_i = \underbrace{\text{Education}_i}_{X_{i,1}}\, \beta_1 + \underbrace{\text{Ability}_i}_{X_{i,2}}\, \beta_2 + U_i
  $$

- $\beta_1$: return to education; $\beta_2 > 0$.

- Suppose $X_1^\top X_2 > 0$:
  $$
  X_1^\top X_2 = \sum_{i=1}^n \text{Education}_i \cdot \text{Ability}_i \ > 0
  $$

- Sign of the bias, three positive factors:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{Bias} &= \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}}_{+}\ \underbrace{X_1^\top X_2}_{+}\ \overset{+}{\beta_2} \ > 0 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \E{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} > \beta_1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Return to education over-estimated.

# Variances of the long and short estimators

## Two conditional variances

- We will use, for $\Gamma$ a function of $X_1, X_2$:
  $$
  \Var{\Gamma U \mid X_1, X_2} = \Gamma\, \Var{U \mid X_1, X_2}\, \Gamma^\top
  $$

- Short regression, by Assumption 3:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \Var{\beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \beta_2 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top U \mid X_1, X_2} \\
  &= \Var{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top U \mid X_1, X_2} \\
  &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top\, \underbrace{\Var{U \mid X_1, X_2}}_{=\,\sigma^2 I_n}\, X_1 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Long regression:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \Var{\beta_1 + (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2 U \mid X_1, X_2} \\
  &= \Var{(X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2 U \mid X_1, X_2} \\
  &= (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2\, \sigma^2 I_n\, M_2 X_1 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \quad (M_2^\top = M_2) \\
  &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \underbrace{X_1^\top M_2 M_2 X_1}_{=\,X_1^\top M_2 X_1} (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Larger variance for the long regression

- **Claim.** For $\beta_2 \ne 0$:
  $$
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} - \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} \ \ge\ 0 \quad \text{(p.s.d.)}
  $$

- Difference of the two variances:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} - \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} - \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 \big[ (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} - (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \big]
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Need to show:
  $$
  (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} - (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \ \ge\ 0
  $$

## Proof, step 1: inverses to matrices

- Scalars $a, b > 0$:
  $$
  b - a \ge 0 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \frac{1}{a} - \frac{1}{b} \ge 0
  $$

- **Claim** (homework). For $A$, $B$ p.d.:
  $$
  B - A \ge 0 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad A^{-1} - B^{-1} \ge 0
  $$

- Apply the homework claim, $A$ and $B$ p.d. by Assumption 4:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & \underbrace{(X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}}_{A^{-1}} - \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}}_{B^{-1}} \ \ge\ 0 \\
  \Longleftrightarrow\quad & \underbrace{X_1^\top X_1}_{B} - \underbrace{X_1^\top M_2 X_1}_{A} \ \ge\ 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Proof, step 2: $X_1^\top P_2 X_1$ p.s.d.

- Rewrite the difference, $I_n - M_2 = P_2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  X_1^\top X_1 - X_1^\top M_2 X_1 &= X_1^\top (I_n - M_2) X_1 \\
  &= X_1^\top P_2 X_1, \qquad P_2 = X_2 (X_2^\top X_2)^{-1} X_2^\top
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $P_2$ p.s.d. $\Longrightarrow$ quadratic form of $X_1^\top P_2 X_1$ p.s.d., for $c \in \mathbb{R}^{k_1}$:
  $$
  c^\top X_1^\top P_2 X_1 c = w^\top P_2 w \ \ge\ 0, \qquad w = X_1 c
  $$

- Therefore:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & X_1^\top X_1 - X_1^\top M_2 X_1 = X_1^\top P_2 X_1 \ \ge\ 0 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} - (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \ \ge\ 0 \quad \text{(step 1)} \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & \boxed{\ \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} - \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} \ \ge\ 0\ }
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Why controlling for $X_2$ increases the variance

- $X_1^\top M_2 X_1$ in terms of $\tilde X_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  X_1^\top M_2 X_1 &= \underbrace{X_1^\top M_2^\top}_{\tilde X_1^\top}\, \underbrace{M_2 X_1}_{\tilde X_1} \quad \text{(symmetric, idempotent)} \\
  &= \tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\tilde X_1 = M_2 X_1$: residual from regressing $X_1$ on $X_2$.

- Conditional variances of $\hat\beta_1$ and $\tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 (\tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1)^{-1} \\
  \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $X_1^\top X_1$ against $\tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1$, from step 2:
  $$
  X_1^\top X_1 - \tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1 \ \ge\ 0
  $$

- $\tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1$: variation of $X_1$ not explained by $X_2$.

- Adding $X_2 \ \Longrightarrow\ $ variance $\uparrow$.

## Bias against variance

- If $\beta_2 \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_1 &:\ \text{unbiased, larger variance} \\
  \tilde\beta_1 &:\ \text{biased in general, smaller variance}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Estimates from repeated samples, $k_1 = 2$; cross at the true $\beta_1$:

  ```{r}
  #| echo: false
  #| results: asis
  #| fig-align: center
  #| fig-width: 6
  #| fig-height: 3.2
  #| fig-dpi: 300
  build_frames("bias-var-build", "omitted-bias-variance", 1:2,
               c("Long regression: estimates spread widely around beta_1",
                 "Short regression added: estimates tight and centred away from beta_1"),
               6, 3.2, function(step) bias_variance_picture(step))
  ```

## Mean squared error (MSE)

- $\underset{1\times 1}{\hat\theta}$: estimator of $\underset{1\times 1}{\theta_0}$.

- Expected loss, add and subtract $\E{\hat\theta}$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{(\hat\theta - \theta_0)^2} &= \E{\big( \hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta} + \E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0 \big)^2} \\
  &= \E{(\hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta})^2} + (\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0)^2 \\
  &\qquad + 2\, \E{(\hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta})(\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0)}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Cross term, $\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0$ not random:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{(\hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta})(\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0)} &= (\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0)\, \underbrace{\E{\hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta}}}_{=\,0} \\
  &= 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Therefore:
  $$
  \boxed{\ \underbrace{\E{(\hat\theta - \theta_0)^2}}_{\text{MSE}} = \underbrace{\E{(\hat\theta - \E{\hat\theta})^2}}_{\Var{\hat\theta}} + \underbrace{(\E{\hat\theta} - \theta_0)^2}_{\text{Bias}^2}\ }
  $$

- A biased estimator can have a smaller MSE.

# Estimated variances

## Two estimated variances

- Long regression, $\hat U = Y - X_1 \hat\beta_1 - X_2 \hat\beta_2$:
  $$
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) = s^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}, \qquad s^2 = \frac{\hat U^\top \hat U}{n - k}
  $$

- Short regression, $\tilde U = Y - X_1 \tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) = \tilde s^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}, \qquad \tilde s^2 = \frac{\tilde U^\top \tilde U}{n - k_1}
  $$

- Standard errors, $j$-th entries:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{std. err}\big(\hat\beta_{1,j}\big) &= \sqrt{s^2 \big[(X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}\big]_{jj}} \\
  \text{std. err}\big(\tilde\beta_{1,j}\big) &= \sqrt{\tilde s^2 \big[(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}\big]_{jj}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Third lecture: $\E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2$.

- Sums of squared residuals, in every sample:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat U^\top \hat U &= \|Y - X_1 \hat\beta_1 - X_2 \hat\beta_2\|^2 \\
  &\le \|Y - X_1 \tilde\beta_1\|^2 \\
  &= \tilde U^\top \tilde U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- In terms of $s^2$ and $\tilde s^2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  s^2 &= \frac{\hat U^\top \hat U}{n - k} \\
  \tilde s^2 &= \frac{\tilde U^\top \tilde U}{n - k_1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Two estimated variances, factor by factor:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) &= \underbrace{s^2}_{\E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} \,=\, \sigma^2}\ \underbrace{(X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}}_{\text{bigger}} \\
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) &= \underbrace{\tilde s^2}_{\E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} \,\ge\, \sigma^2}\ \underbrace{(X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}}_{\text{smaller}}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Proof that $\mathrm{E}[\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2] \ge \sigma^2$

- $M_1$, third lecture:
  $$
  M_1 = I_n - X_1 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top
  $$

- $M_1$: symmetric, idempotent, p.s.d., $M_1 X_1 = 0$, $\operatorname{tr}(M_1) = n - k_1$.

- $\tilde U$ under the true model:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde U &= Y - X_1 \tilde\beta_1 \\
  &= M_1 Y \\
  &= M_1 \big( X_1 \beta_1 + X_2 \beta_2 + U \big) \\
  &= \underbrace{M_1 X_1}_{=\,0}\, \beta_1 + M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U \\
  &= M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- We will use, for $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^n$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  (a + b)^\top (a + b) &= a^\top a + b^\top b + \underbrace{b^\top a + a^\top b}_{=\,2 a^\top b} \\
  &= a^\top a + b^\top b + 2\, a^\top b
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Sum of squared residuals:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde U^\top \tilde U &= \big( \underbrace{M_1 X_2 \beta_2}_{a} + \underbrace{M_1 U}_{b} \big)^\top \big( M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U \big) \\
  &= \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + U^\top M_1 U + 2\, \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 U \quad (M_1^\top M_1 = M_1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Conditional mean of $\tilde U^\top \tilde U$ term by term, trace argument (third lecture):
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{\tilde U^\top \tilde U \mid X_1, X_2} &= \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + \underbrace{\E{U^\top M_1 U \mid X_1, X_2}}_{=\,\sigma^2 \operatorname{tr}(M_1)\,=\,\sigma^2 (n - k_1)} \\
  &\qquad + 2\, \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1\, \underbrace{\E{U \mid X_1, X_2}}_{=\,0} \\
  &= \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + \sigma^2 (n - k_1)
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Divide by $n - k_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \frac{\E{\tilde U^\top \tilde U \mid X_1, X_2}}{n - k_1} \\
  &= \boxed{\ \sigma^2 + \frac{\beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2}{n - k_1}\ } \\
  &\ge \sigma^2 = \E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\tilde s^2$: biased upward in general.

# Including an irrelevant regressor

## Irrelevant regressor: both estimators unbiased

- True model, estimated by the long regression $Y \mid X_1, X_2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & Y = X_1 \beta_1 + X_2 \beta_2 + U, \quad \beta_2 = 0 \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & Y = X_1 \beta_1 + U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Short regression:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde\beta_1 &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top \big( X_1 \beta_1 + U \big) \\
  &= \beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Conditional mean of $\tilde\beta_1$, by Assumption 2:
  $$
  \E{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \beta_1
  $$

- Long regression:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_1 &= (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2 \big( X_1 \beta_1 + U \big) \\
  &= \beta_1 + (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top M_2 U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Conditional mean of $\hat\beta_1$, by Assumption 2:
  $$
  \E{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \beta_1
  $$

## Irrelevant regressor: variances

- Same conditional variances as for $\beta_2 \ne 0$, by Assumption 3:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \\
  \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- By the Claim on the larger variance of the long regression:
  $$
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} - \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} \ \ge\ 0
  $$

- $\tilde s^2$ and $s^2$ both unbiased, trace argument, $\operatorname{tr}(M_1) = n - k_1$, $\operatorname{tr}(M_X) = n - k$:
  $$
  \E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2
  $$

## Two cases: $\beta_2 \ne 0$ and $\beta_2 = 0$

- Suppose $X_1^\top X_2 \ne 0$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \text{a. } \beta_2 \ne 0 \ \Longrightarrow\ & \tilde\beta_1:\ \text{biased in general} \\
  \text{b. } \beta_2 = 0 \ \Longrightarrow\ & \hat\beta_1:\ \text{larger variance than } \tilde\beta_1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

# Orthogonal regressors

## Orthogonal blocks: $M_2 X_1 = X_1$

- Suppose $X_1^\top X_2 = 0$:
  $$
  X_1^\top X_2 = 0 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \text{columns of } X_1 \in S^\perp(X_2)
  $$

- Then:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  M_2 X_1 &= X_1 - P_2 X_1 \\
  &= X_1 - X_2 (X_2^\top X_2)^{-1} \underbrace{X_2^\top X_1}_{=\,0} \\
  &= X_1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Exactly orthogonal dummies, high school (HS) and college (C), $k_1 = k_2 = 1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  X_{i,1} &= \mathbf{1}(\text{Education}_i = \text{HS}) \\
  X_{i,2} &= \mathbf{1}(\text{Education}_i = \text{C})
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Never both equal to $1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  & X_{i,1}\, X_{i,2} = 0 \quad \text{for every } i \\
  \Longrightarrow\quad & X_1^\top X_2 = \sum_{i=1}^n X_{i,1}\, X_{i,2} = 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

## Same estimate, same variance

- Estimators coincide, by $M_2^\top = M_2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \hat\beta_1 &= \big( X_1^\top \underbrace{M_2 X_1}_{=\,X_1} \big)^{-1}\, \underbrace{X_1^\top M_2}_{=\,(M_2 X_1)^\top =\, X_1^\top}\, Y \\
  &= (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top Y \\
  &= \tilde\beta_1
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Both unbiased:
  $$
  \E{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \E{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \beta_1
  $$

- Equal conditional variances:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \\
  &= \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $X_1^\top M_2 X_1$ against $X_1^\top X_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  X_1^\top X_1 - X_1^\top M_2 X_1 &\ge 0 \\
  X_1^\top M_2 X_1 &= X_1^\top X_1 \quad \text{if } X_1^\top X_2 = 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Adding $X_2$ with $X_1^\top X_2 = 0 \ \Longrightarrow\ $ variance unchanged.

## Which regression to run

- $X_1^\top X_2 = 0$; two options: long $Y \mid X_1, X_2$, short $Y \mid X_1$.

- Short regression's error:
  $$
  Y = X_1 \beta_1 + \underbrace{X_2 \beta_2 + U}_{V}
  $$

- $M_1 X_2 = X_2$, by the same chain as $M_2 X_1 = X_1$.

- Short regression's residuals keep $X_2 \beta_2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde U &= M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U \\
  &= X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\tilde U$ in terms of the long regression's fit, $\hat\beta_1 = \tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \tilde U &= Y - X_1 \tilde\beta_1 \\
  &= Y - X_1 \hat\beta_1 \\
  &= X_2 \hat\beta_2 + \hat U
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $X_2 \hat\beta_2$: not removed from $\tilde U$.

## Controlling for orthogonal $X_2$: smaller estimated variance in general

- $\E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2}$ with $M_1 X_2 = X_2$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} &= \sigma^2 + \frac{\beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2}{n - k_1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 + \frac{\beta_2^\top X_2^\top X_2 \beta_2}{n - k_1} \\
  &= \sigma^2 + \frac{\|X_2 \beta_2\|^2}{n - k_1} \\
  &> \sigma^2 = \E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} \quad \text{if } X_2 \beta_2 \ne 0
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Estimated variances, same estimate $\hat\beta_1 = \tilde\beta_1$:
  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) &= s^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} \\
  \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) &= \tilde s^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- Short regression's estimated variance: biased upward if $X_2 \beta_2 \ne 0$.

- $\Longrightarrow$ Use $\hat\beta_1$, the long regression.

- Fourth and fifth lectures: std. err $\downarrow \Longrightarrow$ confidence interval length $\downarrow$, power $\uparrow$.

# Summary

## Omitted and irrelevant regressors

- In every sample: $\tilde\beta_1 = \hat\beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \hat\beta_2$; equal if $X_1^\top X_2 = 0$.

- $\E{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \beta_1 + (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1} X_1^\top X_2 \beta_2$, bias $= 0$ if $\beta_2 = 0$ or $X_1^\top X_2 = 0$; $\E{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \beta_1$.

- $\Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1} = \sigma^2 (\tilde X_1^\top \tilde X_1)^{-1}$, $\Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}$.

- $X_1^\top X_1 - X_1^\top M_2 X_1 = X_1^\top P_2 X_1 \ge 0 \Longrightarrow \Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} - \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} \ge 0$.

- $\beta_2 \ne 0 \Longrightarrow$ $\hat\beta_1$ unbiased, larger variance; $\tilde\beta_1$ biased in general, smaller variance.

- $\text{MSE} = \Var{\hat\theta} + \text{Bias}^2$.

- $\beta_2 = 0 \Longrightarrow$ both unbiased, $\hat\beta_1$ larger variance; $\E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2$.

## Estimated variances and orthogonal regressors

- $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) = s^2 (X_1^\top M_2 X_1)^{-1}$, $s^2 = \hat U^\top \hat U / (n - k)$; $\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}\big(\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2\big) = \tilde s^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}$, $\tilde s^2 = \tilde U^\top \tilde U / (n - k_1)$; $\hat U^\top \hat U \le \tilde U^\top \tilde U$.

- $\tilde U = M_1 X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U$; $\E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 + \beta_2^\top X_2^\top M_1 X_2 \beta_2 / (n - k_1) \ge \sigma^2 = \E{s^2 \mid X_1, X_2}$.

- $X_1^\top X_2 = 0 \Longrightarrow M_2 X_1 = X_1 \Longrightarrow \hat\beta_1 = \tilde\beta_1$ and $\Var{\hat\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \Var{\tilde\beta_1 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 (X_1^\top X_1)^{-1}$.

- $X_1^\top X_2 = 0$, $X_2 \beta_2 \ne 0 \Longrightarrow$ $\tilde U = X_2 \beta_2 + M_1 U$, $\E{\tilde s^2 \mid X_1, X_2} = \sigma^2 + \beta_2^\top X_2^\top X_2 \beta_2 / (n - k_1) > \sigma^2 \Longrightarrow$ use $\hat\beta_1$, the long regression.
